country.comment: Examines 53 municipalities across the Colombian departments of Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda.
country.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF p. 6, Catastro y SGP; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos (Figura 1)

effect_estimate.comment: Cadastral updating alone did not consistently raise property tax revenue, SGP water/sanitation transfers, aqueduct coverage, or water quality, though two-thirds of analyzed municipalities experienced post-update increases in sewerage subscribers and coverage (unadjusted for secular time trends).
effect_estimate.value: Using municipality-level robust paired-samples t-tests (alpha = 0.05) comparing 5-year periods before and after cadastral updating: (1) total property tax collection increased significantly in 27/53 municipalities (50.94%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.80) and per-capita property tax in 29/53 municipalities (54.72%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.69); (2) national SGP drinking-water and basic-sanitation transfers increased significantly in 13/52 municipalities (25.00%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.81); (3) aqueduct subscribers increased significantly in 8/33 municipalities (24.24%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.77) and aqueduct coverage (subscribers/cadastral parcels) in 5/33 municipalities (15.15%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.82); (4) sewerage subscribers increased significantly in 22/33 municipalities (66.67%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.56) and sewerage coverage in 22/33 municipalities (66.67%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.56); and (5) the Water Quality Risk Index (IRCA) showed no significant change in 30/42 municipalities (71.43%) and increased significantly (higher risk) in 12/42 municipalities (28.57%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.87).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 9–16, Resultados and Tablas 2–7; PDF p. 17, Conclusiones

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (documented statistical/descriptive association): the study tests unadjusted pre-post statistical differences in aggregate municipal administrative datasets without a credible quasi-experimental control group (Serious/Critical confounding risk under ROBINS-I, precluding 3) and without directly observing how cadastral records or tax revenues operated administratively to connect households or expand water/sewerage networks (PDF p. 17 notes lack of detailed process explanation as a limitation).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 6–7, Metodología y Datos; PDF pp. 11, 16–17, Resultados and Conclusiones

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines municipal cadastral updating and parcel valuation/property taxation (property), territorial/multipurpose cadastral planning and SSPD coverage certification for fiscal targeting (planning), and central-local intergovernmental fiscal/institutional coordination via SGP water and sanitation transfers (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 5–7, Impuesto Predial, Catastro y SGP, Metodología y Datos; PDF pp. 11, 16–17, Resultados and Conclusiones

outcome_flags.comment: Measures registered utility subscribers (suscriptores de acueducto y alcantarillado, i.e., formal connections), piped water and sewerage utility access/coverage (cobertura de acueducto y alcantarillado proxy = subscribers / cadastral properties), and drinking-water quality risk (Índice de Riesgo de Calidad del Agua - IRCA).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 6–7, Metodología y Datos (Fórmula 1); PDF pp. 11, 13–16, Resultados and Tablas 5–7

publication_year.comment: Published in Bitácora Urbano Territorial, Vol. 34, No. 1, Marzo - Junio 2024, pp. 97-114 (received 21/10/2023, accepted 26/12/2023).
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and citation block

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Evaluates a specific administrative intervention (municipal cadastral updating) using longitudinal pre-intervention vs. post-intervention municipal data (5 years before vs. 5 years after each municipality's update year). Appraised under ROBINS-I as a non-randomized before-after intervention study, with Serious/Critical risk of bias due to lack of an untreated comparator group to account for secular trends in utility expansion and revenues.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF pp. 6–8, Metodología y Datos and Tabla 1

sample_size.comment: Unit of analysis is the municipality observed over two 5-year periods (pre- vs. post-cadastral update). Subsamples vary by data availability in administrative platforms (note Tables 2, 3, 4, and 7 truncate printed rows on pp. 9–10, 12, and 15, while text on pp. 11 and 16 states exact analyzed municipal totals: 53, 53, 52, 33, and 42).
sample_size.value: 53 municipalities across 3 departments (Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda) observed over two 5-year periods (10 years per municipality within 2000–2020); analytic subsamples: 53 municipalities for property tax, 52 municipalities for SGP water/sanitation transfers, 33 municipalities for aqueduct and sewerage subscribers and coverage, and 42 municipalities for water quality risk index (IRCA)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1; PDF pp. 11 and 16, Resultados

study_design.comment: Evaluates municipal indicators across two 5-year periods (before and after each municipality's staggered cadastral update year between 2004 and 2015) using municipality-by-municipality Shapiro-Wilk normality tests and Robust Paired Samples T-Tests (JAMOVI Walrus library) with Cohen's d effect sizes, without an untreated control group or multivariable adjustment.
study_design.value: Longitudinal uncontrolled before-and-after (pre-post) municipal quantitative study using robust paired-samples t-tests
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF pp. 6–7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1
